title: Rural bank branches and poverty in India: Burgess and Pande (2005)
estimand: Effect of rural bank expansion on the rural poverty headcount ratio (percentage points), 2SLS with instruments from the 1977-1990 branch-licensing rule; each panel measures bank expansion differently.

options.label: Rural branches per capita
options.justification: BP Table 3 (baseline).

options.label: Rural credit share
options.justification: BP Table 4 instruments the rural share of credit with the same rule.

options.label: Rural savings share
options.justification: BP Table 4 instruments the rural share of savings with the same rule.

options.label: Post-1976 and post-1989 trends
options.justification: BP baseline: both breaks of the 1:4 licensing rule.

options.label: Post-1976 trend only
options.justification: Leave one instrument out: the post-1989 trend enters as a control, relaxing its exclusion restriction (BP Table 3 column 6 uses the 1977 break alone).

options.label: Post-1989 trend only
options.justification: Leave one instrument out: the post-1976 trend enters as a control (BP Table 3 column 7 uses the 1990 break alone).

options.label: Initial-condition trends
options.justification: BP baseline: 1961 population density, rural share and income, interacted with the same trends and breaks.

options.label: Break terms only
options.justification: The identifying variation is the trend break in 1961 branches; other initial conditions are omitted.

options.label: Plus policy controls
options.justification: BP Table 5: land reform, health and education spending, other development spending.

options.label: Plus policy and political controls
options.justification: BP Table 5: party shares in state legislatures.

reference.source: Burgess and Pande (2005), American Economic Review 95(3), Table 3, column 3 (2SLS, N = 627)

notes: Every specification reports the Montiel Olea-Pflueger effective first-stage F under the same clustered covariance. 16 clusters (15 when a state is left out); confidence intervals use t critical values with G-1 degrees of freedom. Policy controls are missing for some state-years, so those specifications use fewer observations, as in BP Table 5.
